body.statement:
Let \(w_1,\ldots,w_N\in[0,1]\) be fixed, and let \(A\) be a uniformly random subset of \(\{1,\ldots,N\}\) of fixed size \(n\geq1\).  Then, for every \(t>0\),
\[
\Pr\!\left(\left|n^{-1}\sum_{i\in A}w_i-N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^Nw_i\right|\geq t\right)
\leq2\exp(-2nt^2).
\]

source.locator: Section 6, Theorem 4 and the ensuing sampling-without-replacement consequence
source.verbatim_statement: If the function f(x) is continuous and convex then E f(sum X_i) <= E f(sum Y_i).

attestation.note: Verified against Hoeffding (1963), Section 6, Theorem 4, printed page 28, equation (6.2), in the JSTOR scan hosted by Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute at https://www.cs.rpi.edu/academics/courses/spring06/random/hoefding.pdf; X is sampling without replacement and Y sampling with replacement as defined immediately above.
